Definition: from G2596 and G691; to be (render) entirely idle (useless), literally or figuratively:--abolish, cease, cumber, deliver, destroy, do away, become (make) of no (none, without) effect, fail, loose, bring (come) to nought, put away (down), vanish away, make void.
BiblicalUsage: To render idle is to abolish and make useless, and Paul says our old man is crucified that the body of sin might be destroyed, and charity never faileth, and the last enemy that shall be destroyed is death, and whoever seeks to be justified by the law is fallen from grace. The word undoes what stands against God: sin, death, and the law's claim on us.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Christ has abolished the power of sin and will abolish death itself, and that is the victory I live in. I hold that love never fails because it is the one thing death cannot destroy, and I will build my life on what lasts.
